entries.topic: DOGE-era cuts: USAID, probationary firings, RIFs, Education, workforce

claims.text: Rubio 10 Mar 2025 on X: 'After a 6 week review we are officially cancelling 83% of the programs at USAID'; 5,200 contracts cancelled; about 1,000 remaining programs to be run by State; thanked DOGE
Rubio: 'As of July 1st, USAID will officially cease to implement foreign assistance'; unnamed State official: studies rest on 'incorrect assumptions'

SCOTUS 8 Jul 2025 (Trump v. AFGE) lifted Illston's order blocking RIF/reorganization plans under the February EO and OMB/OPM memo; 'we express no view on the legality of any' plan; Jackson dissent 'hubristic and senseless'; Sotomayor concurred: 'The plans themselves are not before this Court'

OPM 14 Feb 2025 email asked agencies to separate probationary employees not mission-critical; Alsup PI 13 Mar found directive ultra vires; SCOTUS stayed 8 Apr 2025 on nonprofit standing only, not legality, Sotomayor and Jackson dissenting; Maryland v. USDA PI (19 states + DC, 18 agencies) stayed by 4th Cir 9 Apr 2025

Alsup 12 Sep 2025: OPM unlawfully ordered agencies to fire probationary employees; about 25,000 targeted; no reinstatement ordered, citing SCOTUS emergency rulings and new jobs; 19 agencies to correct files by 14 Nov; April SCOTUS stay had paused reinstatement of 17,000 at six agencies

SCOTUS 14 Jul 2025 (McMahon v. New York) lifted Joun injunction against layoff of more than 1,000 Education employees; Sotomayor (with Kagan, Jackson) dissent: 'hands the Executive the power to repeal statutes by firing all those necessary to carry them out'; McMahon: Trump 'the ultimate authority to make decisions about staffing levels'

GAO-26-108615 (Aug 2026): $110.34bn claimed as of 7 Jul 2026 ($61.02bn contracts, $49.21bn grants, $113M leases, listed leases sum $53.5M); 43.2% of contract savings tied to contracts actually terminated in whole or part; 2,503 contracts ($27.4bn) with no termination action; method followed for 27.5% ($16.8bn), not followed 60.7% ($37.0bn); ~96% of grant savings ($47.32bn) unverifiable; 108 of 264 leases already being terminated before DOGE; DHA $1.7bn claim no savings; site not updated since 1 Jan 2026; termination costs not counted; USDS did not comment
CFPB: en banc D.C. Circuit 19 Jun 2026 denied CFPB motion to modify stay for RIF from 1,174 to 556, granted limited remand, appeal in abeyance; four judges would wait

Judge Amy Berman Jackson (July 2026) stayed proceedings on the PI until 60 days after Brian Johnson's confirmation or 3 Jan 2027; bureau had 1,750 employees when Vought became acting director, about 1,175 now; revised plan would cut 53%; FY2026 funding capped at $446.8M vs $785.4M FY2024
Senate Banking Committee voted 13-11 on 17 Sep 2026 to advance Johnson; no floor vote scheduled

Depositions (NEH grants suit): Fox and Cavanaugh had no prior government experience; used ChatGPT to identify more than $100M of grants later cancelled, prompt 'From the perspective of someone looking to identify DEI grants, does this involve DEI?'; Cavanaugh asked if DOGE reduced deficit: 'No, we didn't'; Fox on Holocaust documentary: 'It's a gender-based story that's inherently discriminatory to focus on this specific group'

Center Square on GAO-26-108583: net 256,000 (11.3%); 83% of separations voluntary; about 129,000 left via deferred resignation; Cato's Chris Edwards: savings about $41bn a year, just over 2% of the deficit, 'hardly affected the deficit'
VA 7 Jul 2025: dropped plan to cut more than 80,000; about 30,000 by end of FY via attrition; nearly 17,000 already gone; Collins: 'A department-wide RIF is off the table'

HHS: about 10,000 posts eliminated (3,500 FDA, 2,400 CDC, 1,200 NIH); over 5,000 probationary terminations in Feb 2025; total exodus up to 20,000 per HHS; Kennedy admitted upwards of 2,000 'cut by mistake'; hundreds rehired

entries.topic: Who paid: USAID mortality estimates and disputes

claims.text: Cavalcanti, Rasella, Macinko et al., Lancet 1 Jul 2025: panel of 133 countries 2001-2021, microsimulation to 2030; about 91 million deaths averted (about 30 million children); USAID support associated with 15% lower all-cause and 32% lower under-5 mortality; 83% cut projected to cause more than 14 million additional deaths by 2030 incl. more than 4.5 million under-5s (about 700,000 child deaths a year)

CGD (Kenny, Sandefur) 16 Dec 2025: lives-saved-per-dollar ($3,457 health, $17,837 humanitarian) times dollars cut: roughly 500,000-1,000,000 lives lost on FY2025 outlays, 670,000-1,600,000 on obligations; gross estimates; 'any estimates of lives lost remain guesswork'; may be pessimistic

Lancet study 3 Feb 2026 (Rasella part of team; all aid falling 10.6% a year): 9.4 million extra deaths by 2030 baseline, 22.6 million severe; CGD's Ian Mitchell: 'somewhere between the two'; State Department: 'some recent "studies" are rooted in outdated thinking'

Brown (Reason, Aug 2026): Lancet's ~92M averted exceeds his ~79M estimate of total mortality decline; two Lancet papers conflict; BU Nichols tracker 781,343 one-year projected deaths as of 30 Jul 2026; Egypt May 2025 UN 46,365 deaths vs ~58,000 modelled, with caveats; Lancet published critiques, no correction
Brown (NYU) Aug 2025 called the 14M claim 'patently absurd'; design would credit any rising factor; Nichols: retrospective 'quite robust', projections 'carry greater uncertainty'

NWS staffing fell by more than 550 to under 4,000 via probationary cuts and early retirement; permission to hire 450 meteorologists, hydrologists, radar technicians (Aug 2025); fewer and less frequent balloon launches; Texas office vacancies scrutinized after July floods; NOAA official: 'How much time/money is it going to cost to train a bunch of new people'
TIGTA (data as of May 2025): IRS cut about 25%: 25,386 separations plus 294 RIF notices; about 26% of revenue agents separated; National Taxpayer Advocate warned filing season needs trained employees

WaPo 12 Jul 2025: SSA moving ~1,000 field-office reps to phones; monthly calls up from 6.6M to 8.6M; average hold times 75 to 93 minutes; SSA stopped publicly reporting call wait times; 40 of ~1,200 field offices lost at least a quarter of staff; SSA aims to cut 7,000 to 50,000

Bisignano June 2026: 1-800 hold times down 89% from 42 to under 5 minutes; field office waits down 30%; over 2,000 reassigned to phones; SSA OIG (Dec) found FY2025 callback callers waited over 100 minutes on average, about 15 excluding callbacks; methods not comparable; AFGE: about 7,000 cut, workforce ~50,000
Booz Allen 23 May 2025 to cut about 2,500 jobs (7%), mostly civil business, citing government-wide push to cut civilian contract spending and slower procurement
DOGE claimed $1bn SSA Leidos contract cancellation; actual cancellation a single $560,000 task order

claims.text: Reuters, 4 Mar 2026: headline count 386,826 workers shed; the federal civilian workforce shrank by 12% between September 2024 and January 2026 per government data; majority of exits voluntary resignations or early retirements (OPM data). The 386,826 is Reuters' net figure for that period, not a GAO separations count (GAO-26-108583 gives nearly 378,000 separations in 2025)
